title: Model Gatekeeper: staged A/B rollout and auto-rollback orchestration
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Purpose: Build a repeatable A/B testing framework ("Model Gatekeeper") for model version rollouts that supports staged canaries, controlled exposure, shadow traffic validation, automated statistical checks and deterministic auto-rollback. The goal is to give product/platform teams a low-friction path to validate changes in output quality and regression risk, while providing clear operational controls and auditability.

Scope: experiment configuration UI + API, traffic scheduler (percent and cohort), sequential and fixed-horizon statistical tests, safety gates (content/regression monitors), shadow validation pipeline, auto-rollback policies, incident hooks and observability dashboards. This ticket is the cross-functional PM spec and rollout plan; ENG will own infra work items and DES will provide UX mocks (linked in comments).
acceptance_criteria: 1) PM/ENG spec merged and signed off; 2) API for experiment creation supports: model_variant list, exposure_percent, cohort_rules, duration or sequential stopping rules, baseline selection; 3) Console surfaces experiment with live exposure and key metrics (latency, cost, accuracy/regression signals); 4) Statistical checking engine supports at least one sequential test (alpha-spending) and one Bayesian credible-interval check; 5) Auto-rollback triggers correctly revert traffic, annotate rollout, and create incident ticket; 6) Shadow traffic path can be enabled per experiment without affecting production latencies; 7) Pilot with two internal teams completed and post-mortem captured.
implementation_notes: Decisions so far: prefer sequential testing (alpha spending / O'Brien-Fleming style) for long-running exposures to reduce required sample size and allow early stopping; provide Bayesian posterior overlap as an optional metric for teams preferring probabilistic statements. Use trellis-based routing to assign cohorts (hashing on token/customer_id) to avoid skew. KV-caching and batching heuristics must be respected for canaries. Auto-rollback will have two modes: conservative (immediate rollback on high-severity safety alert) and permissive (rollback only after statistical confirmation). Policy config stored in existing rollout service (ENG-4124).
metrics: Primary experiment metrics: user-visible quality signal (task-specific — e.g., F1, BLEU surrogate, or custom eval score), high-severity safety violations (per 1000 requests), latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, completion rate/errors. Secondary: token distribution drift, prompt-category breakdown, and model confidence proxies. All metrics must be emitted to Console and MetricsDB with experiment tags.
statistical_checks: Supported checks: sequential frequentist (alpha-spending boundary), fixed-horizon t-test / proportion test, Bayesian posterior probability (P(variant > control) > threshold), uplift band checking (min delta). Configurable thresholds per experiment; default: early-stop if p<0.01 with minimum sample of 10k requests for primary metric. Risk trade-off: sequential tests reduce runtime but are sensitive to peeking; will provide warnings and auto-enforce alpha schedule.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot) — internal-only: shadow validation + 1% canary for 2k requests/day for 2 weeks; Phase 2 (Beta) — 5% exposure across 3 cohorts for 1 week with sequential checks enabled; Phase 3 (General) — ramp to target traffic with pre-approved rollback policies. Rollout automation will annotate release and write audit logs. Pilot owners: Marco Silva (ENG), Leah Park (DES for console flows), Aisha Rahman (PM).
ui_changes: Console: new 'Experiments' tab with quick-create wizard, exposure timeline, live metric cards, safety alerts, and one-click rollback. Experiment detail view with cohort map and rollout annotation timeline. API: POST /v1/experiments, PATCH for policy updates; GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results. DES has initial mocks: link in comments.
risks_mitigation: Risk: statistical false positives -> mitigation: conservative default alpha and min-sample; require two independent signals before auto-rollback on non-safety metrics. Risk: latency regressions in canary -> mitigation: isolate canary to nodes with reduced batching and provide fallback routing. Risk: misconfigured experiments causing over-exposure -> mitigation: quota guard rails, approval flow for >10% exposure, per-customer rate limits.
